description: We are fourth-year college students and STEM alumni, studying Computer Science & Physics and Mechanical Engineering, with skills in coding, data analysis, engineering, and 3D design. We also have knowledge of physics, astrophysics, fluid mechanics, and thermodynamics. We aim to explore NASA’s microgravity combustion data and seek teammates in AI, machine learning, data science, visualization, and web development
summary: ZERO FLARE — FLAME EVIDENCE LAB turns NASA's underused microgravity-combustion archive into a live, evidence-grounded research environment for the Artemis generation. We ingested 24 NASA PSI combustion investigations — recovering 22 experimental tables (2,009 rows, SHA-256-verified against the acquisition manifest), 63 verified equations, and honest model cards — and built an AI research copilot, CIR-1, that answers every factual claim through 26 deterministic tools with visible provenance, never inventing data. Researchers explore investigations, run a comparability gate that refuses invalid cross-study claims, screen lunar/ISS/Mars habitats with a transparent facility-risk engine, walk a 3D equipment lab built from public NASA descriptions (plus official NASA ISS & Perseverance 3D assets), and export reproducible evidence packets. Missing data stays missing; negative results stay visible.
details:
ZeroFlare Evidence Lab - Start your Mission

1-Home page

This interface is the main dashboard of the ZERO FLARE platform. It provides access to NASA microgravity fire research, experimental datasets, investigations, scenarios, comparisons, 3D tools, and scientific resources. The homepage also highlights key research statistics, available environments such as ISS and Earth reference conditions, and provides direct access to the CIR-1 AI copilot for research assistance.

2-Mission

This interface presents the main research environments used in ZERO FLARE, including the International Space Station, lunar habitat, Mars habitat, and spacecraft cabin. Users can select an environment to explore how gravity, oxygen level, and atmospheric conditions affect fire behavior and combustion research.

This interface evaluates whether the selected environment stays within the limits of available microgravity combustion data. It compares oxygen level, pressure, and material-family test ranges, then highlights where the selected conditions are supported by experiments and where they fall outside the tested envelope.

This interface guides users to start from the available evidence. It provides direct access to investigations, comparisons, and scenarios, while clearly showing the limits of the platform, including unsupported predictions, missing media, and areas without validated experimental data.

This interface visualizes the evidence coverage across NASA combustion investigations. It shows which research dimensions—such as gravity, oxygen, pressure, material, hardware, outcomes, and measurement context—are observed, reported, condition-specific, or missing from the current dataset.

This interface presents curated NASA research videos and experimental media related to microgravity combustion. It allows users to explore visual evidence from real space-based fire experiments, including flame behavior, droplet combustion, and laboratory testing aboard the International Space Station.

 

This interface summarizes key findings from the available microgravity combustion evidence and ranks important scientific results with their supporting datasets and limitations. It also provides access to authentic NASA imagery related to combustion experiments, allowing users to connect research conclusions with real experimental media.

 

 3- investigations

This interface provides access to the available combustion investigations and their detailed research workspaces. Users can click any experiment in the investigation list to open it and explore its objectives, data, equipment, media, equations, graphs, metadata, related investigations, and research keywords.

This interface provides a visual analysis of the selected experiment’s dataset. It presents column statistics, data distributions, scatter plots, and condition-based comparisons, helping users quickly identify patterns, relationships, and important characteristics within the experimental measurements.

This interface displays authentic NASA images related to the selected combustion investigation. It allows users to explore real experimental hardware, laboratory setups, researchers, and spaceflight equipment, providing visual context for the scientific data and investigation results.

This interface provides the verified scientific equations related to the selected investigation. It organizes gas laws, pressure calculations, mixture properties, stoichiometry, and flammability equations, with references and direct links to use them inside the Scenarios workspace.

This interface presents a visual evidence graph showing the selected investigation and its related experiments, equipment, and research connections. Users can click any connected investigation node to open that experiment and return directly to its Overview page for further exploration.

 4- scenario

This interface supports fire-safety scenario analysis across the full lifecycle, from prevention and detection to prediction and suppression. Users can configure the environment, compare compartment risk levels, review facility screening results, and save scenario settings for further analysis.

 

This interface combines the CIR-1 Fire Safety Assistant with verified equations, prevention evidence, and scientific calculators. Users can ask questions about the selected facility, explore supporting NASA evidence, calculate atmospheric and flammability conditions, and review research gaps before making scenario-based decisions.

5- compareThis interface compares experimental conditions across multiple investigations. It visualizes observed ranges, such as oxygen concentration, and helps users identify where different studies overlap, differ, or may not be directly comparable before making cross-investigation conclusions. 6- 3D lab

This interface provides an interactive 3D laboratory for exploring spacecraft combustion hardware and experimental apparatus. Users can browse hardware records, view reconstructed equipment models, inspect components, access related NASA media, and explore animated experiment demonstrations.

This interface provides a detailed 3D view of the selected combustion apparatus, including labeled components, related experiment information, and authentic NASA images. It also includes an animated experiment demonstration that shows the main stages of the procedure, allowing users to better understand how the hardware and experiment operate.

7-Data and Resources

This interface documents the data sources used across ZERO FLARE. It shows the recovered experimental tables, row and column counts, duplicate records, parse issues, file sizes, investigation IDs, and verification hashes, providing a transparent view of the project’s data provenance and integrity.

8- Chatbot

These interfaces show the CIR-1 Research Copilot in both compact and expanded views. The assistant is available across the platform to help users ask questions about experiments, datasets, equations, models, and NASA combustion evidence, while keeping the conversation connected to the current research context.

This interface shows CIR-1 responding to a research question about a specific investigation. The copilot retrieves experiment information such as the investigation title, research area, project type, objectives, and supporting references, allowing users to explore NASA combustion studies directly through natural-language questions.

Benefits

  •  Provides a centralized platform for exploring NASA microgravity combustion research, experimental datasets, scientific equations, and supporting media.
  • Makes complex fire-science information easier to understand through interactive dashboards, visualizations, comparison tools, and 3D representations.
  • Helps researchers explore individual NASA investigations in detail, including objectives, datasets, equipment, media, equations, graphs, and documented gaps.
  •  Allows users to compare multiple experiments and identify similarities, differences, overlapping conditions, and limitations before making cross-study conclusions.
  • Supports evidence-based analysis by connecting results to verified datasets, NASA records, scientific equations, and provenance information.
  • Uses the CIR-1 AI Research Copilot to answer natural-language questions about investigations, datasets, equations, models, and research evidence.
  • Reduces the time required to manually search through multiple research records and datasets.
  •  Helps users identify missing data, unsupported assumptions, and areas where additional experiments may be required.
  •  Supports scenario-based analysis for different environments such as the International Space Station, lunar habitats, Mars habitats, spacecraft cabins, and Earth-reference conditions.
  • Provides fire-safety scenario support across prevention, detection, prediction, and suppression stages.
  • Includes scientific calculators and verified equations that can be used directly inside research scenarios.
  • Provides interactive data analysis, including descriptive statistics, distributions, relationships, grouped comparisons, and correlation analysis.
  •  Supports the exploration of authentic NASA research media to provide visual context for combustion experiments and experimental hardware.
  • Provides interactive 3D models of combustion hardware and experimental apparatus to improve understanding of complex equipment.
  • Maintains transparency by clearly displaying data provenance, source references, duplicate records, parse issues, and evidence limitations.
  • Preserves missing information instead of automatically replacing it with artificial values.
  • Helps students, researchers, and engineers understand microgravity combustion research in a more accessible and interactive way.
  • Provides a single research environment that combines data analysis, scientific evidence, visualization, AI assistance, and engineering tools.
  • Supports faster and more informed research decisions by bringing multiple sources of evidence into one platform.
  • Can be extended in the future with additional datasets, experiments, scientific models, and AI capabilities.
  • Provides a web-based interface that can be accessed without requiring users to install specialized scientific software.
  • Encourages traceable and reproducible research by linking calculations and results back to their original sources.
  • Helps distinguish between experimentally observed results, reported information, condition-dependent evidence, and missing evidence.
  • Reduces the risk of presenting unsupported scientific conclusions by clearly identifying the tested limits of available data.
  • Creates an educational environment that can also support demonstrations, research presentations, and academic projects.

Development Tools

  • Next.js – Main full-stack web framework used to build the ZERO FLARE platform and server-side API routes.
  • React – Used to build reusable and interactive user-interface components.
  • TypeScript – Provides strong typing, safer development, and improved maintainability.
  • Node.js – Server-side JavaScript runtime used by the application and development environment.
  • npm – Used to install and manage project dependencies and development packages.
  • Google Gemini API – Powers the CIR-1 AI Research Copilot and natural-language interaction.
  • Google GenAI SDK (@google/genai) – Provides official server-side access to Gemini, structured responses, and native function calling.
  • Zod – Used for validating API requests, responses, tool arguments, and structured application data.
  • REST API Architecture – Used to connect the frontend, AI agent, scientific tools, and application services.
  • Next.js API Routes – Used to provide secure server-side endpoints such as the CIR-1 copilot API.
  • CSV Data Processing – Used to store and process the cleaned experimental datasets supplied by the research team.
  • JSON – Used for structured configuration, API responses, reports, tool outputs, and metadata.
  • Custom Data Query Layer – Used to filter, group, analyze, and calculate statistics from the experimental datasets.
  • Statistical Analysis Tools – Used for descriptive statistics, grouping, median calculations, correlations, and experimental-data exploration.
  • Scientific Equation Registry – Used to manage and execute verified scientific formulas throughout the platform.
  • BM25 Information Retrieval – Used to search and rank research evidence and knowledge-base documents.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) – Used to provide the AI assistant with relevant research evidence and source context.
  • Native AI Function Calling – Allows Gemini to select and execute validated ZERO FLARE research tools.
  • Structured AI Responses – Used to provide predictable and validated outputs from the AI assistant.
  • HTML5 – Provides the structural foundation of the web interface.
  • CSS / Responsive Styling – Used to create the visual design, space-themed interface, and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript – Supports interactive browser behavior and application logic.
  • Interactive Data Visualization – Used to display charts, distributions, comparisons, and experimental relationships.
  • 3D Visualization Technologies – Used to display interactive combustion hardware and apparatus models.
  • NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Data – Provides the main experimental research evidence used by the platform.
  • NASA Images and Video Library – Provides authentic NASA imagery and research media.
  • Git – Used for version control and tracking changes across development phases.
  • GitHub – Can be used for private source-code storage, collaboration, backup, and deployment integration.
  • Visual Studio Code / Coding Agents – Used for development, debugging, code inspection, and implementation support.
  • Codex / AI Coding Assistance – Used to support structured implementation, testing, debugging, and code review during development.
  • Automated Testing – Used to verify equations, dataset queries, API contracts, request isolation, provider integration, and user-interface behavior.
  • TypeScript Type Checking – Used to identify type errors before deployment.
  • Production Build Testing – Used to verify that the application can successfully compile and run in production mode.
  • Environment Variables (.env.local) – Used to securely configure private server-side settings such as AI API credentials.
  • Vercel – Intended as the deployment platform for the production Next.js application.
  • Porkbun – Used for management of the custom project domain and DNS configuration.
  • Custom Domain (zero-flare.study) – Intended as the final public address of the ZERO FLARE platform.
  • HTTPS / SSL – Used to provide secure communication between users and the deployed web application.
  • Browser-Based Speech Synthesis – Used to provide optional voice output for the CIR-1 Research Copilot.
  • Responsive Web Design – Allows the platform to adapt to different screen sizes and presentation environments.
  • Hash-Based Data Integrity Verification – Used to confirm that imported research files remain unchanged and traceable.
  • Provenance Tracking – Used to preserve the relationship between displayed results, experimental datasets, and original research sources.
  • Server-Side Secret Management – Prevents private AI API credentials from being exposed in the browser or public application code.
